title: Minimum Absolute Difference Queries
summary: The minimum absolute difference of an array is the smallest difference between any two distinct elements.
statement: The minimum absolute difference of an array is the smallest difference between any two distinct elements. For a given array and queries, calculate the minimum absolute difference for each subarray defined by the queries. If all elements in a subarray are identical, the difference is -1. Return an array of results corresponding to each query.
constraints: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and every value is from 1 through 100.
There are at most 20000 inclusive [left,right] queries with left < right.
For each range, compare distinct values; return -1 when fewer than two distinct values occur.
hints: The small value bound allows a prefix-frequency table for values 1 through 100.
For each query, scan values in order and test presence by subtracting two prefix counts.
The minimum difference must occur between consecutive present distinct values.
Prefix subtraction exactly identifies the range's value set, and sorted consecutive gaps contain the minimum pairwise distance.
editorial: Prefix subtraction exactly identifies the range's value set, and sorted consecutive gaps contain the minimum pairwise distance.

tests.explanation: The distinct-value gaps in the four ranges are 2, 1, 4, and 1.
The first range has only value two, while the other minimum gaps are 1, 1, and 3.
